corpus: mixed human/model final text from earlier sessions
finding: Useful primary personal advantage over base and pooled is excluded under both interval methods. Useful donor advantage is excluded under writer resampling but remains unresolved under crossed writer/prompt resampling. Useful uniform advantage remains unresolved under both. Every primary interval includes zero, so no primary advantage, disadvantage or parity is established. Residual donor useful advantage is excluded only under writer resampling; residual pooled useful advantage remains unresolved under both methods. Both residual model-rival intervals include zero. Residual uniform performance is worse under both methods. Raw base and pooled useful advantages are excluded under both methods, while raw donor useful advantage is excluded only under writer resampling; all raw model-rival intervals include zero. Raw sums are worse than uniform under both methods.
limits: Mixed human/model training provenance, sparse histories, shared units, one larger-model seed and transferred rank preclude independent human confirmation, backbone or corpus ranking, general personal-learning limits and private-goal inference. Other matrix cells remain unfinished; failed and unknown predecessors remain separate.
